The City Commission meets on the first and third Tuesday of the month, unless otherwise noted in the schedule. The agendas are posted [online](https://www.valleycity.us/commission/city-commission-meetings) prior to the meeting.

CSi Cable Services replays the meetings on Cable Channel 68. BEK Communications replays on BEK Channel 26.

You can receive email notification when the agendas are posted. Please contact Judi Hintz to be added to the listserv at [jhintz@valleycity.us](mailto:brandy.johnson@valleycity.us)

### City Commission Policies

### Deadline for Submitting Agenda Items for City Commission Meetings

All agenda items discussed at a regular City Commission meeting shall be submitted to the office of the City Auditor of the City of Valley City by 5 PM on a Wednesday prior to that City Commission meeting.

*Resolution No. 1877, adopted October 15, 2012*

### Rules of Order &amp; Decorum Applicable to Speaking at Regular Open Meetings of the Valley City Commission

1. No longer than five minutes will be allowed for presentation of any agenda item to the Commission by an individual other than a City official or employee, unless additional time is given by the presiding officer or by a majority vote of the City Commission. The comments will be relevant to and focused upon the agenda item.
2. General public participation and comment apart from agenda items will be scheduled for all regular open meetings. A five minute time limit will also apply to such participation and comment. Those wishing to speak must place their name and the subject to be addressed on a sign in sheet prior to the meeting. The presiding officer will allow comment if the subject matter is considered relevant to current city business.

**Authority:**

Legal opinions of the North Dakota Attorney General

2007-0-11  
2003-0-07  
1999-0-07  
1998-0-17  
1998-F-11

affirm that the open meetings law is to give members of the public access to meetings, but not the right to participate in or speak at the public meeting. Further, the public body may adopt reasonable rules and policies to insure orderly conduct and behavior at its public meetings.

*Adopted May 19, 2008*
